extracted.intended_audience: Recipients of HHS Federal financial assistance (health care providers, State Exchanges), OCR-regulated entities, legal counsel, and civil rights advocates
extracted.subtask_description: Final-rule guidance and procedural requirements for administrative enforcement, exemption requests, complaint handling, and related OCR processes under Section 1557 of the ACA. Covers how recipients request and receive religious/conscience exemptions, OCR timelines, enforcement procedures, complaint processes, and the treatment of Medicare Part B as federal financial assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurance of Exemption Notification Requirements (§92.302(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient that seeks assurance regarding the application of particular provision(s) of the part to specific contexts, procedures, or health care services must submit a notification in writing to the Director of OCR. The notification must include (1) the particular provision(s) of this part to which the recipient objects; (2) the legal basis supporting the assurance of exemption request, including the standards governing the applicable conscience or religious freedom law; and (3) the factual basis supporting the recipient's view that it is exempt, including identification of the conflict between the recipient's conscience or religious beliefs and the application of a provision in this part, which may include the specific contexts, procedures, or health care services that the recipient asserts will violate their conscience or religious beliefs overall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notification may be provided at any time, including before an investigation is initiated or during the pendency of an investigation. The written notification is the mechanism that triggers the temporary exemption described in §92.302(c). OCR encourages recipients to provide public notice if they choose but does not require recipients to publish their own notifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary Exemption upon Notification (§92.302(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient's notification and request for an assurance of an exemption to OCR will trigger the extension of a temporary exemption to the recipient covering the period of time it takes OCR to reach a determination on the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The temporary exemption applies only to the provision(s) as applied to the specific contexts, procedures, or health care services identified in the recipient's notification and will exempt conduct that occurs during OCR's review and determination. If there is an investigation or enforcement activity related to the specific provisions for which an assurance is requested, the temporary exemption serves as a defense through the investigation or until OCR has made a determination or through the administrative appeal process if invoked. OCR will work promptly to reach a determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR Timetable for Review (email acknowledgement within 30 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: For pre-enforcement requests for an assurance of an exemption, OCR shall provide the recipient with email confirmation within 30 days of the recipient's notification acknowledging receipt of their request and stating that OCR will work expeditiously to reach a determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request is received during the pendency of an investigation, the temporary exemption shall serve as a defense to the relevant investigation or enforcement activity until the final determination of the recipient's request, the conclusion of the investigation, and any relevant appeal. The temporary exemption shall exempt the recipient from the provision of care at issue in the investigation until a final determination is made or during the pendency of any appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of an Assurance of Exemption (§92.302(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: An assurance of an exemption exempts the recipient from OCR's administrative investigation and enforcement with regard to the application of a particular provision, as applied to the specific contexts, procedures, or health care services provided in the written determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The exemption assurance will not apply to all contexts, procedures, or health care services. Outside the scope of the granted exemption assurance, a recipient must otherwise have a legitimate, nondiscriminatory reason for denying or limiting service, and any such decision must not be based on unlawful animus or bias or constitute a pretext for discrimination. Example provided: a hospital with an exemption to not provide sterilizations may not rely on the exemption to broadly decline unrelated services, e.g., cancer treatments, to any individual if the hospital otherwise provides that care.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Appeal Process for Adverse Determinations (§92.302(e)-(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients subject to an adverse determination of their request for assurance of an exemption may appeal OCR's determination. Recipients may raise their request before an administrative hearing examiner from the Department with the procedural protections outlined under 45 CFR part 81.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The temporary exemption granted under §92.302(c) remains in effect until completion of the administrative appeal process. A determination under this section is not final for purposes of judicial review until after a final decision under 45 CFR part 81.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and Transparency of Exemption Determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters recommended OCR publish all determinations for exemptions claimed or granted—proposing inclusion of recipient name(s), factual basis, OCR's analysis, and specific provisions—possibly within 10 days and accompanied by links to relevant documents; commenters argued this would improve transparency for providers and patients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR declines to require affirmative publication of exemption requests or determinations in §92.302 but notes nothing in the final rule prevents a recipient from providing public notice and encourages recipients to do so. OCR is subject to FOIA and information may be released consistent with FOIA and agency regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction Between OCR Assurances and Private Rights of Action
rubrics_metrics.description: The §92.302 process applies to OCR investigations and enforcement but does not address private lawsuits; a temporary or final assurance of an administrative exemption from OCR does not itself preclude any private lawsuit under section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient can still raise applicable Federal religious freedom or conscience laws as a defense in private litigation, and where OCR has assured an exemption the recipient could argue that assurance is evidence that a Federal religious or conscience law likely applies in private litigation. OCR would not open or continue an investigation under section 1557 against the recipient regarding compliance with the provision for which an assurance has been requested while a temporary exemption is in effect or after a final determination granting an exemption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption of Title VI Procedures for Administrative Enforcement (§92.303(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The procedural provisions applicable to title VI (45 CFR 80.6 through 80.11 and part 81) are applied with respect to administrative enforcement actions against health programs and activities of recipients and State Exchanges concerning discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or any combination thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This means complaints alleging age discrimination or multiple bases will be subject to the same procedural provisions as other bases rather than a separate Age Act mediation requirement. The text was revised to add the phrase “or any combination thereof” throughout to acknowledge intersectional claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of Mandatory Age Act Mediation Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The final rule removes the proposed §92.303(b) which would have applied Age Act mediation procedures (including mandatory referral to mediation under 45 CFR 91.43) to age-based complaints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR determined the Age Act mediation requirement is not required by statute and opted for consistent procedures across section 1557 administrative enforcement. Complainants who wish to mediate may still be provided the option to do so under the Age Act procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint Filing Deadline and Extensions (180 days)
rubrics_metrics.description: A complaint must be filed no later than 180 days from the alleged discrimination, consistent with the enforcement mechanisms under title VI adopted for section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will continue to extend the 180-day filing deadline for good cause as outlined in the title VI regulation at 45 CFR 80.7(b). To make this information widely available, OCR is reinstating a required Notice of Nondiscrimination (§92.10), which includes information on how to file a complaint with OCR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessible Complaint Mechanisms and Support Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Commenters urged that the final rule offer clear, fully accessible complaint mechanisms (plain language directions, FAQs, process diagrams, alternative formats, ASL videos, and complaint processes for individuals with limited English proficiency (LEP)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR currently offers resources and has updated its Civil Rights Discrimination Complaint Form and Portal (including the form/portal in fifteen languages other than English and additional clarity on reportable forms of discrimination). OCR will consider further changes to simplify and improve accessibility on an ongoing basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship Status Irrelevant to Filing or Enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Citizenship or immigration status is not relevant to an enforcement process or the ability to file a complaint with OCR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An individual's citizenship or immigration status does not prevent or alter their ability to file a complaint or OCR's ability to enforce potential violations under section 1557.

rubrics_metrics.name: OCR Compliance Reviews and Title VI Compliance Information Requirements (§92.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR conducts compliance reviews in addition to complaint-driven investigations (e.g., based on news reports or other information). Section 92.303 adopts 45 CFR 80.6 (Compliance information) requirements, including cooperation, assistance, records maintenance, access to pertinent records, and sharing information with the public regarding protections against discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR acts as a neutral factfinder and does not presume discrimination by a covered entity. Compliance reviews are part of robust enforcement and may include requiring covered entities to produce records and demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral of Complaints Outside OCR Jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: If OCR receives a complaint over which it does not have jurisdiction, it shall promptly notify the complainant and shall make reasonable efforts to refer the complaint to the appropriate Federal Government entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This new provision replaces the former age-discrimination related provision and formalizes OCR's practice of notifying and referring out-of-jurisdiction complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement Remedies, Monitoring, and Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement mechanisms include Voluntary Resolution Agreements and Settlement Agreements resulting from investigations; such agreements generally include a monitoring period and reporting requirement to ensure ongoing compliance. If a recipient or State Exchange does not come into voluntary compliance and is found in violation, OCR can take compliance action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR may initiate fund termination proceedings under 45 CFR 80.8 or use any other means authorized by law, including referral to DOJ for enforcement proceedings. Monitoring and reporting requirements are intended to ensure continuing compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for Claims Against the Department and Prohibition on Department Retaliation (§92.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims of discrimination against the Department under section 1557 are subject to the procedures in the section 504 federally conducted regulation at 45 CFR 85.61 and 85.62; the Department is prohibited from retaliating against an individual or entity for asserting rights under section 1557 or participating in an investigation, proceeding, or hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory text is revised to include discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability, or any combination thereof. OCR will provide technical assistance and be proactive in enforcing Department-administered programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medicare Part B Considered Federal Financial Assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department concludes that Medicare Part B funding meets the definition of “Federal financial assistance” when received by providers and suppliers, such that Part B payments are considered Federal financial assistance with respect to title VI, title IX, section 504, the Age Discrimination Act, and section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change in interpretation does not alter the longstanding regulatory definition of “Federal financial assistance,” but it means providers who receive only Part B payments are now covered as recipients subject to the applicable civil rights obligations. The Department sought comment on the time allowed for such recipients to come into compliance and on resources the Department can provide to assist newly covered entities.
